meta.title: Ceiling is price × possible customers
meta.summary: SAMPLE $20/mo × 10k users = $200k/mo. A $150k cost base is tight vs $5k.

success.message:
Session complete. Ceiling = price × possible customers; compare cost scale to that ceiling.

SAMPLE: $200k/mo vs $150k (tight) vs $5k (room).

start.message:
SAMPLE: $20/mo, maybe 10k customers. Instant feasibility?

First number?

choices.label: Start with server invoices and never size the ceiling
20 × 10k × 12 in the first breath and lose the monthly

wrong_start_cost_first.message:
Smell test is ceiling vs cost scale. Price × reachable customers first.

Return to the ceiling.

wrong_start_yearly.message:
You can yearly later. Monthly ceiling vs monthly cost is the conversation unit.

Return to the ceiling.

cost.message:
Infra already $150k/mo against a $200k ceiling.

Read?

choices.label: Tight — cost already rivals the ceiling
Fine — $50k leftover is a fat margin
$150k cost means revenue must already be $150k

wrong_cost_fine.message:
25% leftover before people, ads, and support is not fat. The model is weak at this cost scale.

Revisit the read.

wrong_cost_impossible_math.message:
Cost is not revenue. The ceiling is $200k if you get all 10k.

Revisit the read.

choices.label: Room to operate — cost is a small slice of $200k
Still tight because 10k users is 10k users

wrong_check_same.message:
User count did not change; cost scale did. $5k vs $200k is a different story.

Try the check again.

wrong_check_zero.message:
Do not equate cost and revenue.

Try the check again.
